subject: Renewal options and next steps to move GreenLeaf to Azure Marketplace
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Porter <emily.porter@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal: option to convert invoicing to Azure Marketplace

Hi Emily —

Hope you had a good week. GreenLeaf’s annual renewal for our inference platform is coming up on April 18. Based on our earlier call, I wanted to outline the path to move your invoicing from direct to Azure Marketplace before that renewal date. The benefits we discussed: consolidated invoicing for your cloud team, streamlined procurement approvals via marketplace entitlements, and simplified seat/usage alignment across subscriptions.

Quick next steps I recommend so we can keep your renewal uninterrupted:
- Agree to conversion in principle (we handle contract amendment)
- Confirm billing owner and PO workflow for Azure Marketplace (procurement team)
- Sign the marketplace amendment / complete listing entitlement map

I’m attaching a short checklist that covers timelines and the typical docs procurement asks for. If it helps, Ben (cc’d) can run a short call with your procurement/legal to walk through the amendment and any change to discounts. Are you available for a 30-min call tomorrow or Friday?

Thanks,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_marketplace_conversion_checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

From: Emily Porter <emily.porter@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@greenleafhealth.com>, procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal: option to convert invoicing to Azure Marketplace

Hi Steph —

Thanks for the note and the checklist. We’re interested in moving to the Marketplace but have a few questions from procurement and finance before we commit:

1) Does the Marketplace path change the renewal date or create a gap?
2) How do discounts and committed spend translate to marketplace SKUs?
3) We need to confirm whether we can continue to use the same cost center mapping in Azure billing exports.

We can do a call Friday (3/5) at 10am ET. I’ll loop Tom (finance) and procurement on the call. I also attached a spreadsheet of procurement questions to this thread.

Best,
Emily
Emily Porter
Director of Product Ops, GreenLeaf Health
Attachment: GLH-procurement-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 45KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Porter <emily.porter@greenleafhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal: option to convert invoicing to Azure Marketplace

Hi Emily —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions. I’ll cover these on our call but wanted to put concise answers in writing so procurement has a record:

1) Renewal timing: moving to Marketplace does not require you to change the effective service date. We’ll execute a marketplace amendment that aligns the marketplace entitlements to your existing term so there’s no gap. If you prefer, we can target the marketplace billing to start at the next invoice cycle (no service interruption).

2) Discounts / committed spend: Marketplace uses SKU-level entitlements. We’ll provide a mapped SKU list that preserves your committed discount as a marketplace price adjustment; we’ll include the committed volume terms in the amendment so your unit economics remain intact.

3) Cost-center mapping: Azure exports will show the invoice line items by SKU; finance can map SKU IDs to cost centers. We’ll add an extra column with SKU IDs and recommended cost-center tags when we send the entitlement spreadsheet.

Logistics for Friday: 10am ET works for us. On the call: Steph (AE) will confirm customer success transition details, Laura (legal, cc’d) will cover amendment mechanics, and Jordan (billing ops, cc’d) will provide the SKU mapping and timeline for the marketplace activation.

High-level ask after the call: procurement confirms billing owner email and the PO cadence (monthly vs. annual).

Meeting invite attached; dial-in in the invite.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Strategic Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

- Please include the anticipated first marketplace invoice amount (estimatation) so our cash planning team can forecast.
- We need the DocuSign-ready amendment by next Monday (3/8) to route through our legal queue.

Tom / Emily —

Following up with the items you requested:

1) Estimated first invoice: based on last 12 months usage and the SKU mapping I’ll send, we estimate the first Marketplace invoice will be approximately $58,000 (this assumes current committed discount is applied as a marketplace price adjustment). That’s a ballpark; we’ll provide a detailed line-item estimate when we share the SKU file.

2) DocuSign amendment: we’ve prepared the amendment and I can send the DocuSign link by end of day Monday 3/8. The amendment language preserves the current term dates and records the transition of invoicing to Azure Marketplace; it also includes an explicit clause preserving the committed discount schedule.

Next items from my side: I’ll attach the SKU mapping CSV and a one-page vendor note for your accounts payable team. Expect those first thing Monday. If anything else is needed to get the PO routed, flag it and I’ll expedite.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
